1.explanation: The React NumberInput component class (in NumberInput.js) defines the overall markup and icon buttons via its render() method; to offer alternate controls you must adjust render() (and potentially the translation IDs it uses). Its getDerivedStateFromProps enforces value capping around the min/max props and will need to stay in sync with any new control mechanism. In the plain JS version, NumberInput._handleClick binds to the up/down icon elements and houses the logic to change the value when those are clicked; to support different control patterns you would extend or override _handleClick (or add new handlers) to drive value changes from whatever alternate UI you introduce.
1.bug_scenario: The user story shows the Carbon NumberInput rendered with only the default up/down caret icons for incrementing and decrementing the value. The request is to explore alternative control options beyond those carets (for example, custom buttons, sliders, or other UI affordances) so the existing caret‐only UI is too restrictive.

2.explanation:
There are two parallel implementations that render and wire up the up/down caret controls:

• In the React package (packages/react/src/components/NumberInput/NumberInput.js), the NumberInput class’s render() method is where the CaretUpGlyph and CaretDownGlyph (or other icons) are output alongside the input. To introduce new control options you must update or replace that render logic (and any associated SVG/Icon imports).

• In the vanilla-JS package (packages/components/src/components/number-input/number-input.js), the NumberInput class wires click handlers in its constructor and _handleClick method against elements with the .up-icon/.down-icon classes. Any alternative controls (e.g. plus/minus buttons or a slider) will need changes there to query the new elements and perform the same step logic.
2.bug_scenario: In the Carbon NumberInput control (React + vanilla-JS implementations), the only way to increment or decrement the value is via the small up/down caret icons on the right. The screenshot shows the “Number Input” label above a text field showing “50” and two caret glyphs for stepping the value. The issue requests exploring alternative control styles (e.g. buttons, sliders, steppers) instead of—or in addition to—those carets.
